headline: Team Problem-Solving Discussion Activity for ESL Classes
outcomes: Students collaborate in English to generate, evaluate, and defend solutions to realistic problems
Practise the language of brainstorming — suggesting, building on ideas, evaluating feasibility
Develop adaptability by responding to mid-activity complications that invalidate initial solutions
Build teamwork vocabulary and group decision-making discourse in an authentic communication context
howItWorks: The AI presents a problem with limited resources and a clear success condition related to your topic
Teams brainstorm solutions in English and submit their plan via the group device
Partway through, the AI introduces a complication — a resource loss, a new constraint, an unexpected obstacle
Teams must revise and defend their adapted solution, practising the language of justification under pressure
teacherUseCases: Project English practice where students must plan, present, and defend in a collaborative setting
Problem-solution writing preparation — generating and evaluating ideas before drafting
Teamwork and communication skills for professional English or business classes

faq.a: The teacher assigns teams manually or lets LessonCaptain auto-assign based on how many students have joined the session. Teams of 3–5 work best for productive discussion without any student going silent.

faq.q: What kinds of problems are generated?
faq.a: Problems are matched to your topic. A business class might problem-solve a product launch with a budget cut. A general English class might plan a community event with limited space and time constraints.

After teams submit their initial plan, the AI introduces a complication — something that removes a resource, adds a stakeholder requirement, or changes the deadline. Teams must update their plan, which creates a second, richer discussion phase.

faq.q: What technology does Problem Solvers require?
faq.a: Each student participates via their phone or tablet in a browser. No download required — the session is accessible from a shared link.

faq.q: Can one team present to the whole class?
faq.a: Yes. After the activity, teams can present their final solution using the board. The teacher can display all team plans simultaneously for comparison and class discussion.
Yes, Problem Solvers is free to run. Students join through a browser link — no accounts or downloads needed.
